name: Abuse of Non-Profit Organisations and Charities for Terrorist Financing
description: Terrorist groups or their supporters may exploit charities and other non-profit organisations by diverting funds, using them as cover for transfers to conflict areas, or infiltrating their governance. Most non-profits are low risk, so controls must be proportionate and avoid de-risking legitimate humanitarian work.

sources.text: FATF, Risk of Terrorist Abuse in Non-Profit Organisations (2014)
FATF, Best Practices on Combating the Abuse of Non-Profit Organisations (Recommendation 8) (2015; revised Nov 2023)
FATF Recommendation 8 and its Interpretive Note

indicators.name: Operations in high-risk areas without credible delivery evidence
indicators.canon: Operations in high-risk areas without credible delivery evidence
indicators.desc: Organisation sends funds to areas with active terrorist presence but cannot evidence projects, beneficiaries, partners or auditable delivery.
indicators.ctx: Organisation sends funds to areas with active terrorist presence but cannot evidence projects, beneficiaries, partners or auditable delivery.
indicators.fp: Humanitarian actors in crisis zones often work through informal channels and face real documentation barriers.

indicators.name: Beneficial owners, trustees or signatories linked to concerning persons
indicators.canon: Ownership or controllers linked to designated or previously reported parties
indicators.desc: Owners, officers or associates match sanctions or designation lists, prior suspicious reports or adverse media.
indicators.ctx: Officers, trustees or major donors appear in adverse media, sanctions or terrorist designation data, or share details with previously reported entities.
indicators.fp: Common names and community roles produce coincidental matches.

indicators.name: Donations structured through cash or anonymous collections
indicators.desc: Donations are made through cash, anonymous collections or structured amounts.
indicators.ctx: Large volumes of cash collection boxes, bucket collections or anonymous donations deposited with no collection records.
indicators.fp: Street collections and community events are cash heavy and lawful.

indicators.name: Funds pass through quickly to personal accounts or unrelated entities
indicators.desc: Funds received into an account are forwarded onward within a very short period, often in near-equal amounts and leaving minimal balance.
indicators.ctx: Charity account receives donations and immediately forwards most funds to individuals, personal accounts or businesses unrelated to stated objects.
indicators.fp: Some charities grant to individuals or use procurement agents.

indicators.name: Activity inconsistent with registered purpose
indicators.desc: Transactions, geographies or counterparties do not match the objects declared in the registration or constitution.
indicators.ctx: Transactions, geographies or counterparties do not match the objects declared in the registration or constitution.
indicators.fp: Charities evolve and respond to emergencies outside their normal remit.

indicators.name: Unregistered or recently de-registered organisation soliciting funds
indicators.canon: Missing, misused or unverifiable licence or registration
indicators.desc: Customer offering a regulated or permitted activity cannot evidence the required licence or registration, or operates under a licence held by another party.
indicators.ctx: Entity collects donations without evidence of registration, or continues after loss of status, regulatory warning or inquiry.
indicators.fp: Small community groups may be exempt from registration thresholds.

indicators.name: Funds routed through intermediaries or informal value transfer in conflict zones
indicators.canon: Funds routed via informal agents or cash couriers into conflict areas
indicators.desc: Funds reach regions with armed groups through informal value transfer, MVTS or cash couriers.
indicators.ctx: Charity uses third-party agents, MVTS or cash couriers to reach recipients where regulated banking is limited, with limited visibility of the final recipient.
indicators.fp: Banking access is genuinely restricted in some crisis settings.

indicators.name: Fundraising claims inconsistent with use of funds
indicators.canon: Fundraising claims inconsistent with use of funds
indicators.desc: Public appeals describe one cause while expenditure patterns show little programme spending or large payments to connected parties.
indicators.ctx: Public appeals describe one cause while expenditure patterns show little programme spending or large payments to connected parties.
indicators.fp: Overhead ratios vary and appeals may legitimately change focus.
